name: Jeff Hafley

views.text: Coverage beliefs like press-man and vision-and-break work from any front; the front is just the shell.
A post safety who controls the middle, takes away big plays and catches the ball is the heart of a defense.
Coaches on a staff liking and backing each other matters more than what they know about X's and O's.
Put players where they can succeed rather than forcing them into a system.
A disciplined team that does not beat itself with penalties gives itself a chance every week.
A physical run game should still work when the defense knows it is coming.
The whole roster should play with the edge of a good defense: more physical than whoever is across from it.
Turn on the tape; effort and toughness show up there before anything else in a prospect.
A new quarterback should grow while staying himself, without a number hung on him.

signatures: talks at length and in detail about coverage technique when given the floor
praises his assistants by name for their character as much as their football minds
explains calling his own defense by pointing to the offensive head coaches he worked for
want: to change Miami's culture into a tough, physical team and win the franchise's first playoff game in a generation as a first-time NFL head coach
fear: that running the whole team and calling the defense leaves both jobs half done
voice: Talkative, upbeat and detailed; he speaks at length about coverage concepts and about toughness and physicality as an identity for the whole team. He talks about his staff warmly and in terms of trust and character, and keeps expectations for individual players loose.

evidence.summary: Introductory remarks: moving Green Bay to a 4-3 but saying his coverage beliefs apply to any front; describes a post safety who controls the middle; says college football has changed with COVID, the portal and NIL. Spoke nearly 30 minutes and addressed criticism of his career. LaFleur says he hired the best fit and wants a fast, physical defense.

On assembling his staff: relationships among coaches matter more to him than X's and O's; he wants coaches who like and support each other; kept two of Joe Barry's assistants and brought others from the NFL and Boston College, praising them for loyalty, intensity and player relationships. Team-written.

evidence.publisher: Green Bay Packers (packers.com), Wes Hodkiewicz and Mike Spofford
evidence.summary: Primer: four seasons as Boston College head coach with three bowl-eligible teams and a defense that led the ACC in fewest penalties; worked on Kyle Shanahan's 49ers staff with Adam Stenavich and under Robert Saleh; NFL secondary coach from 2012; a Siena wide receiver. Facts only.

Introductory Dolphins press conference: he wants a physical run game that works even when expected, will keep calling defensive plays as Shanahan and LaFleur called offense, wants an offense that can run under center, screen and hit explosives; the quarterback decision is left open. Measured, fundamentals-focused remarks.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Dolphins on SI), Dante Collinelli
evidence.summary: He says he fought to bring Sean Duggan from Green Bay over LaFleur's wish to keep him, chose him on merit rather than eight or nine years together, calls him a rising star who frees him to run all three phases, and recalls trusting his booth observations as an Ohio State graduate assistant.

Transcript of his new coordinators' introduction: Slowik calls Hafley a close friend and is grateful to work with him again; Duggan describes deep trust over eight years and says Hafley lets him build the defense around players. Their words about him, not his.

At the league meeting he wants the whole roster as physical and aggressive as his Green Bay defense, says prospects' tape shows whether they love football and play hard, wants Malik Willis to keep growing while staying himself without set expectations, and backs a deal for De'Von Achane. Team-written.
